# GitHub Actions

GitHub's hosted CI. [[labour-fraud-analysis]] carries one workflow, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`,
triggered on every push and pull request — the only CI across the repositories ingested with it.
`ubuntu-latest`, `actions/setup-python@v5` pinned to 3.12 with the pip cache enabled, then six steps.

## The steps, and what each one actually asserts

| Step | Enforces |
|---|---|
| `ruff check src` | lint only |
| `python src/build_db.py` | the SQLite build runs with foreign keys on, so **0 FK violations** across the dataset |
| `build_docs.py` then `git diff --exit-code` on four paths | the committed generated docs match what the data produces — [[generated-docs-checked-by-ci-diff]] |
| `validate_anonymization.py` | structural integrity **plus a regex PII sweep** — and nothing more, see below |
| `pytest -q` | primary-key uniqueness, foreign-key closure, row counts against the manifest, and two signal-preservation tests — [[pytest]] |
| `nbconvert --execute` | the analysis notebook runs end-to-end headless, 240-second timeout |

Two habits here are worth copying. **Step names are assertions, not verbs** — "Build database —
asserts 0 foreign-key violations", "Derived docs are in sync with data/", "Notebook executes
end-to-end". A red build tells you what became false, from the run summary alone, before you open a
log. And **the notebook is executed in CI**, which is rare: a stored notebook is a screenshot of a
result, an executed one is a test of it. See [[reproducible-analysis]].

## The finding: the workflow is more honest than the README

`confidence: high` — interview-confirmed, 2026-07-28.

The README claims no value in the published data identifies a real party, "a claim that is
test-verified in CI". The workflow's own comment says otherwise:

> "On a clean runner the private source + rules are absent, so the leak/stem scans skip and this
> enforces structural integrity + the PII regex sweep."
> — labour-fraud-analysis-a-forensic-data-investigation/.github/workflows/ci.yml, 2026-07-11

Two of the [[disclosure-gate]]'s four checks — the run-time blocklist built from the private corpus,
and the stem guard from a git-ignored rules module — **cannot execute where their inputs do not
exist**. Public CI enforces the other two. This is a general property of secret-scanning gates
rather than a local mistake, and the workflow states it in the place a reader will find it. The
README does not. See [[documentation-drift]].

## Environment gaps CI does not close

- It installs `requirements.txt`, never the package. `pyproject.toml` declares no `dependencies` key
  at all, so `pip install -e .` would install nothing — [[setuptools-and-pyproject]].
- It runs **3.12 only**, while the project declares support from 3.10 and lints to a py310 target.
  The declared floor is never exercised by anything.
- Dependencies are floor-pinned with no upper bound and no lockfile, so a green run today is not
  evidence about tomorrow's resolution.

## Relationship to the Makefile

CI's step list is `make ci` spelled out in YAML rather than invoked — `db docs validate lint test`,
plus lint first and the notebook last. The duplication is small and the [[make]] target is the
documented clean-clone contract, so a developer can reproduce the pipeline locally with one command.
Keeping them in sync is manual; nothing checks that they agree.
